transcript:
User: We have a girl at the front desk, she picks up fine. Not sure why I'd need this.
Agent: Got it, sounds like she’s doing a good job. Mhm—when she’s at lunch, on a break, or already on another call, what happens to the next call that comes in?
User: Janet calls them back when she's free. We don't really track any missed calls.
Agent: Makes sense, a lot of offices work that way. So... roughly, how many calls a week would you guess are ringing through to voicemail or going unanswered before Janet gets back to them?
User: I don't really count, but it's not like it's a big problem. We've managed fine so far.
Agent: Got it, you feel things are working well enough as is. Curious though—when those callers don’t get picked up right away, do you think any of them might just call the next place on Google instead of waiting for Janet’s callback?
User: Possibly, but we've been doing alright. Most people wait for a callback or try again later.
Agent: Yeah, that makes sense, especially if folks already know you. So just to be clear—are you mainly calling today to explore what this is about, or do you feel pretty set with how things are and don’t really want to change anything right now?
User: I'm mostly just exploring right now. We've got a system, and it seems to work for us.
Agent: Gotcha, you’re just checking things out and you feel your current setup works fine. If your call volume were to jump—say busy season or a marketing push—do you think Janet and your current system could comfortably handle a lot more calls without anything slipping through?
User: If things get busier, we might struggle a bit. But we usually manage somehow.
Agent: Mhm, so it works for now, but a spike could get messy. Just so I understand your world better—what kind of business are you running there?
User: We're an auto body shop in Boston, handling repairs and maintenance for all kinds of vehicles.
Agent: Nice, that helps—busy world, lots of calls. So when someone’s in a fender bender or needs a quick estimate and their call doesn’t get picked up right away, does that ever turn into lost jobs, or is that not really something you worry about?
User: We don't worry much. Janet calls back, and most customers wait. It's not a big concern for us.
Agent: Got it, so missed calls don’t really feel like a revenue issue for you right now. Since you’re just exploring, would it be useful if I quickly explained what we actually help auto body shops with, and you can decide if it’s worth thinking about at all?
User: Sure, I'm open to hearing what you offer. Just skeptical about needing it with how we currently operate.
Agent: Totally fair to be skeptical—especially if things feel under control. We help auto body shops make sure every call turns into an estimate or appointment, even when Janet’s busy, so you’re not losing jobs when phones spike or after-hours; if, say, you could turn 20–30 extra calls a month into booked repair work without hiring more staff, would that be interesting at all or still feel unnecessary?
User: Alright, as a backup layer, I can see it. Book your demo. I'm curious now.
Agent: Got it, love that—you’re thinking of it as a safety net. Before we lock in a demo, mind if we do a super quick check on the numbers—just ballpark how many calls a week you think hit voicemail so we can see what’s at stake?
User: We get around 15 missed calls during busy hours weekly. But I suppose it's good to see the numbers.
Agent: Got it, thanks for putting a number to that. And of those 15 missed calls, what percentage do you think would actually turn into a booked job if someone answered live—maybe half, around 50%, or would you put it higher or lower?
User: I'd say around 50% would likely book if we caught them live.
Agent: Makes sense, thanks. And for those jobs that do book, what’s a typical repair ticket worth for you—are we talking more like $400, $650, or closer to $1,000 on average?
User: On average, our repair tickets are around $1,100, so they’re quite valuable to us.
Agent: Right, so those are serious jobs—which is exactly why this matters: based on what you shared, you’re currently leaving about $35,700 a month on the table from calls that don’t get answered live. So… since you’re already curious, how about we do a quick 20‑minute walkthrough this week where we show you exactly how that backup layer would work for your shop—would you rather do it later today or tomorrow?
User: Alright, let's go ahead and book that demo. Tomorrow works better for me.
Agent: Nice, tomorrow’s perfect. First thing—what’s your first name so I know who Jay will be speaking with?
User: It's Dave. Looking forward to seeing how this can help as a backup for us.
Agent: Nice, Dave—thanks for sticking with me through this. And what’s the name of your auto body shop?
User: Kowalski Auto Body in Boston. We've been around a while, so I'm curious how this could support us.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Thanks, Dave! You’re all set for tomorrow at 12:30 your time with Jay to walk through how this can act as a backup layer for Kowalski Auto Body. You’ll get a text message with the confirmation details shortly, and you can add it to your calendar or reschedule from there if you need to. Is there anything else I can help you with before we wrap up?
